$ edit testdata/script/twice.txtar  # restore the settled archive
$ edit testdata/script/twice.txtar  # mark upper's cell of copy, and edit upper's input by hand
$ go test ./b  # tr-b
    script/errs/transform/looped: looped declines the base: the base's do/ tree already errs
    script/garbled/transform/looped: looped declines the base: the base states malformed, which looped neither gives nor keeps
    script/garbled/transform/upper: upper declines the base: the base states malformed, which upper neither gives nor keeps
    script/twice/transform/upper: Uppercases every file under do/out/.
        copy: Does what the case's do/ tree says.
        The cell is frozen by its known gap, gaps line 1: "transform/upper copy Waits on sheets#9."
        Its committed files record today's behavior, and the run now produces different ones:
        transform/upper/out/copy/values.txt differs (-committed +got):
        - A1 SIX
        + A1 SEVEN
        If the gap is closed, remove the line, and the next update writes the cell. If the wrong behavior changed shape, delete the cell's files, and the next update writes them.
    script/twice/transform/upper: Uppercases every file under do/out/.
        A cell of the variant failed, and the archive's inputs for upper's variant differ from what upper makes now:
        transform/upper/in/do/out/values.txt differs (-committed +made):
        - A1 SEVEN
        + A1 SIX
        A normal run reads the inputs, and an update what upper makes. The module's update, FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./..., rewrites them, in the package that owns upper, and the variant's cells but the frozen ones, to which an update only adds an outcome they lack, when their other files match the run and nothing keeps the update from writing them. A normal run checks each frozen cell whose files differ, here copy's, again on the rewritten inputs, against its committed files. If no package owns upper, the root-package check says so, and no update rewrites the inputs.
